author: Today I Found Out
description:
If you’re from Europe or North America, you were probably taught there are four major flavors we can detect: sweet, salty, bitter, and sour. You were also probably taught about the just as false tongue taste map, which in the Bonus Facts later, we’ll get to how that whole ridiculous idea started and made its way into school textbooks despite that any human with a working tongue should have known it was crap.

But going back to the base flavors, if you’re from Asia or watch way too much Food Network, you probably know of a fifth: umami. Usually described as the rich savouriness of meat, seafood, and broth, umami is more technically the taste of a specific molecule found in these foods: glutamate, more familiar to most of us in the form of monosodium glutamate or MSG.

title: The Absolutely Absurd Reason People Think MSG is Bad for You
